text: Which recruitment model should Milestone 3 use?

options.label: Recruit and Replenish orders paid from resources (Option B)
options.rationale: Gives both actions the owner asked for, keeps one order per army, and puts every cost and site in scenario data.

options.label: Diplomacy-style free builds when objectives exceed armies (Option A)
A replacement-point pool spent in a replacement phase, as in Paths of Glory (Option C)
Automatic recovery of men in friendly territory, no cost (Option D)
Drop this idea or defer it

text: Where may a faction recruit new armies?

options.label: Territories tagged for recruitment in scenario data, controlled and uncontested, one new army per territory per turn
options.rationale: Works today: Ceuta, Melilla, La Rioja and the Baleares have no city, and there is no capital field yet.

options.label: Only at a named capital city per territory (a new capitalCityId field)
At any controlled city
Only at the faction's starting (home) sites, as in Diplomacy

text: How long does a new army take to train?

options.label: Per unit type in data: militia 1 turn, infantry, security forces and colonial veterans 2 turns
options.rationale: Simple, data-driven, and reflects that militia columns formed in days while regiments needed cadres.

options.label: Every type arrives at the end of the turn it is ordered
Per type, and longer for stronger types (up to 4 turns for colonial veterans)

text: How should faster militia recruitment for some factions (owner idea 8) work?

options.label: By place: a territory's recruitment entry can shorten militia training there (for example Navarra, Catalunya, Madrid)
options.rationale: Requetes and union militias were local; a place tag changes hands with the ground and needs no faction rule.

options.label: By faction: a faction modifier makes that faction's militia train one turn faster everywhere
No difference between factions

text: When do replenished men arrive, and what does the army do that turn?

options.label: The army holds (no entrenching), men arrive after battles and control; the order fails with a refund if the army fought a meeting or territory battle, retreated, or was destroyed, but standing battles in shared territories do not cancel it
options.rationale: No same-turn combat surprises and attacks stay worthwhile, while armies in shared Asturias and Andalucia can still refill.

options.label: As above, but any battle cancels it, standing battles included (armies in Asturias and Andalucia could almost never replenish)
Men arrive before battles, so they fight that turn
Men arrive after battles even if the army fought

text: How much should replenishing cost compared with recruiting a new army?

options.label: Replenishing costs half as much per value point as recruiting new, capped at half the army's establishment per turn
options.rationale: Rewards keeping veteran armies alive, as Strategic Command reportedly does, without instant full recovery.

options.label: The same price per point either way
Replenishing costs only Manpower; recruiting costs Funds and Manpower

text: Can a destroyed or surrendered army be rebuilt?

options.label: No: it stays gone; a fresh Recruit replaces it with a new id
options.rationale: Keeps the half of M25 that makes destruction matter and keeps unit ids stable for replay.

options.label: Yes: rebuild the named army at full recruit cost at a recruitment site
Yes, but only historical named formations listed in the scenario

text: Which resource set should Milestone 3 use?

options.label: Funds and Manpower, with production capacity as a per-site build limit (Option B)
options.rationale: Two counters, matches the owner's city and rural split and the Republic's men-versus-arms history.

options.label: Funds only (Option A)
Funds, Manpower and Materiel (Option C)
Funds, Manpower, Oil, Food and Political capital (Option D)
Drop this idea or defer it

text: Which of the owner's optional resources should Milestone 3 add as separate counters? Choose all that apply.

options.label: None: fold oil and food into Funds and foreign aid; defer political capital, research and action points
options.rationale: Each one needs upkeep rules or an event system and the owner hedged on all of them.

options.label: Oil, consumed by units each turn
Food, consumed by armies and cities
Political capital, spent on events or foreign aid
Action points per turn (coordinate with idea 6)
Research points

text: How should foreign aid enter the economy?

options.label: A per-faction aid schedule in scenario data: Republic starts with a gold treasury, the insurgent commands receive aid on credit per turn
options.rationale: Moscow gold and Axis and Texaco credit were decisive and give a data-only balance lever.

options.label: No foreign aid: income comes only from the map
Aid as events or cards, deferred to a later milestone
Cities and rural ground, each with its own yield, at the smallest place that exists (city, sub-region, or territory)
options.rationale: Works before and after sub-partitioning (idea 7) and gives the owner's city versus rural split.

options.label: Cities only, like Diplomacy supply centres
Territories only, like Axis and Allies

text: What does a contested territory pay before sub-partitioning exists?

options.label: Its cities pay their controllers; its rural yield pays nobody
options.rationale: Simple and rewards clearing a territory; measured Southern income is 5 Funds under it.

options.label: Its rural yield is split evenly among the factions present
Nothing at all, cities included (the old draft's rule)
They carry over without limit
options.rationale: Easiest to explain; the computer player is told not to hoard, and saving for a big recruit is a real choice.

options.label: They carry over up to a cap per faction
They are lost each turn, as Paths of Glory replacement points are

text: What can players see of each other's economy?

options.label: Balances and income public after each turn; planned spending secret until reveal
options.rationale: Matches the old draft and the simultaneous-orders model without adding fog of war.

options.label: Everything public, including planned spending
Opponents' balances hidden too

text: What should the two new economic actions be called, given that M11 Reinforcement already means a move into friendly ground?

options.label: Recruit (new army) and Replenish (restore men); keep M11 Reinforcement unchanged
options.rationale: Neither word can be read as a move, and the engine's reinforcement-arrived outcome stays valid.

options.label: Raise (new army) and Replace (restore men)
Recruit and Refit
Rename M11 to Redeploy and use Reinforce for restoring men

text: How should the new ruleset relax M25 (no recovery of men)?

options.label: Replace M25 with M28 Replenish in the new ruleset; destroyed armies stay gone; m2-strength keeps M25
options.rationale: Reuses strength and fullStrength as they are and keeps the existing ruleset reproducible.

options.label: Change M25 inside m2-strength itself
Allow both replenishing and rebuilding destroyed armies

text: Does a Replenish order also restore a demoralized army's morale?

options.label: No: only rest recovers morale (M23); a replenishing army does not rest that turn
options.rationale: Keeps men and morale as separate levers, so the player chooses between recovering and refilling.

options.label: Yes: replenishment also clears demoralization
Demoralized armies cannot replenish at all
